brief: Tech positioning has been cut just as NVDA squeezes higher while the broader NDX barely participates. With volatility crushed and NDX still consolidating since May near its 100-day moving average, a close above its shorter-term negative trend line could trigger a broader catch-up squeeze, since prior selling reduced an obstacle to upside. SOX trades weak, near its most oversold RSI since late July, below its 100-day moving average but above its 200-day. The AI debate is shifting from demand to unit economics: Goldman's Privorotsky argues rising demand with falling prices is not automatically bullish if pricing falls faster than consumption grows, though training, HBM and power can stay tight even as inference economics worsen, making the approaching SOX must-hold level important with semiconductor volatility this cheap. DRAM has consolidated with its 21-day moving average turning higher. Hyperscalers are absorbing higher memory costs, which Amazon cited in its latest capex increase, rather than cutting demand, signaling memory suppliers retain pricing power. Separately, BCOM has broken higher and dislocated from its 200-day moving average, moving in tandem with rates. The desk does not want to trade against this momentum but is watching for a further breakout that could revive the inflation narrative.
